Two days ago

It started two days ago.

The intro's wide, held. The night drains out of the room and daylight comes back: two days earlier.

2.2 · 0:04.0–0:09.535→40 mm · f/2.8

Hundreds a day

Ivan was complaining to Claude about how many emails he gets—

Over his shoulder: the inbox fills faster than he can scroll it. The monitor beside it: a calendar packed solid.

2.3 · 0:09.5–0:12.545→48 mm · f/2.4

Too much

hundreds a day, most of them requiring some response.

He sits back and presses the heel of his hand into his brow.

Automate the simple ones

Claude suggested they could automate the simple ones.

Claude's reply streams in, read line by line. Then his answer in the box: yes.

2.6 · 0:21.5–0:24.532→35 mm · f/2.8

2.7 · 0:24.5–0:29.085 mm · f/2

The plan

That was the plan. Review and approve.

The sticky note on the back of his laptop: REVIEW + APPROVE. The focus slips off it to his face.

What else

But once the email system was working, Ivan saw what else was possible.

The pipeline runs on its own. His eyes leave it, to nothing: an idea. The evening comes in.

2.10 · 0:38.0–0:45.020 mm · f/16

Hours

Each one a few hours of coding, a few conversations with Claude to work out the logic.

A time-lapse from across the flat: the sun crosses the floor, night falls, the lamp comes on, day again.

2.11 · 0:45.0–0:50.060→64 mm · f/1.6

Nothing left

Each one removing another task from his daily routine.

His to-do list checks itself off, item by item.

2.12 · 0:50.0–0:54.085→88 mm · f/1.4

Cheat code

The feeling is hard to describe. It's like discovering a cheat code for life.

Very close and still. A small private smile, a nod. Dust hangs in the screen light.

2.13 · 0:54.0–0:59.050 mm · f/2

Hours to minutes

Every problem that used to take hours now takes minutes. Every tedious task can be automated away.

From his shoulder to the clock behind him: the hands spin through hours in seconds, then stop.

2.14 · 0:59.0–1:05.035 mm · f/2.4

Another frequency

Ivan feels like he's vibrating at a different frequency than everyone around him—

The camera circles him. The air has stopped: dust frozen mid-drift. Only he moves.

2.15 · 1:05.0–1:14.028→30 mm · f/4

The door

like he's stepped through a door that others can't even see.

He stands in the open balcony doorway, dawn pouring past him into the dark flat. The light blooms to white.

Light tells the passing days: the same flat at day, evening, sunrise and 3 AM, baked in Cycles and blended in the engine. Times are estimates; every shot is retimed to the voiceover.
